rationale: Pinned route mirroring the hardware-verified sequence from temp_code_test/agentic/minecraft_launch_sequence_test.py: open search, type minecraft, launch it, create a new world, then prove movement/mining/camera/hotbar/inventory controls. Skips LLM planning entirely for this scenario.
assumptions: The Xbox dashboard is the active screen before step 0.
Minecraft is installed or cloud-launchable and appears in search results within the top results row.
The Play button is the first focused item on the Minecraft main menu, and Create New World is directly below it.

steps.intent: Open the Xbox Guide overlay as the entry point into search.
steps.expected_observation: The Xbox Guide overlay appears over the current screen.

steps.intent: Dismiss the Guide overlay before opening search directly.
steps.expected_observation: The Guide overlay closes and the previous screen is visible again.

steps.intent: Open the Xbox global search overlay.
steps.expected_observation: The search overlay is open with the on-screen keyboard visible.

steps.intent: Type the search query using the OCR-verified on-screen keyboard.
steps.expected_observation: The search field contains the text 'minecraft'.

steps.intent: Leave the active search text field so the results list can be navigated with the d-pad.
steps.expected_observation: Focus leaves the search text field while the results list remains visible.

steps.intent: Move focus down from the search field toward the results row.
steps.expected_observation: The highlighted focus has moved down by one row in the search results.

steps.intent: Move focus down again to reach the Minecraft result tile.
steps.expected_observation: The Minecraft result tile is highlighted or is the active launch surface.

steps.intent: Select the highlighted Minecraft result.
steps.expected_observation: The screen begins transitioning away from the search results toward Minecraft.

steps.intent: Confirm launch if a second confirmation prompt appears.
steps.expected_observation: Minecraft begins launching; a splash or loading screen becomes visible.

steps.intent: Wait out cloud sync and the Minecraft loading screen instead of a fixed sleep, until the main menu settles. min_elapsed_seconds prevents settling on the static Mojang splash screen, which is stable for a few seconds before the real main menu loads.
steps.expected_observation: The Minecraft main menu is visible and no longer animating, with the Play button visible.

steps.intent: Press Play on the Minecraft main menu.
steps.expected_observation: The world selection / play menu becomes visible.

steps.intent: Move focus down to the Create New World option.
steps.expected_observation: The Create New World option is highlighted.

steps.intent: Select Create New World.
steps.expected_observation: A world creation confirmation or naming screen becomes visible.

steps.intent: Confirm world creation, reaching the CREATE NEW WORLD settings screen (world name, game mode, difficulty).
steps.expected_observation: The CREATE NEW WORLD settings screen is visible, with the green CREATE button focused.

steps.intent: Press the focused CREATE button on the settings screen to actually create the world and load into it. This is a separate press from step 13, which only reaches the settings screen - pressing A here is what starts world generation.
steps.expected_observation: The CREATE NEW WORLD settings screen closes and the screen begins transitioning to the new world's loading screen.

steps.intent: Wait out the new world's own loading screen instead of a fixed sleep, until gameplay settles. min_elapsed_seconds guards against settling on an early static frame of the loading screen.
steps.expected_observation: The Minecraft world has finished loading; the player's hotbar and crosshair are visible.
steps.stage_goal: Prove the new world loaded into interactive gameplay.

steps.intent: Walk the player forward to prove basic movement.
steps.expected_observation: The player's view has moved, indicating forward movement occurred.
steps.stage_goal: Prove movement and mining controls work in the new world.

steps.intent: Hold the right trigger to start breaking a block in front of the player.
steps.expected_observation: A block-breaking animation or a broken block is visible.
steps.stage_goal: Prove movement and mining controls work in the new world.

steps.intent: Nudge the camera right with a partial-strength stick throw, the same mechanism a human uses to look around.
steps.expected_observation: The player's viewing direction has rotated slightly to the right.
steps.stage_goal: Prove camera control works in the new world.

steps.intent: Cycle the hotbar selection by one slot.
steps.expected_observation: The highlighted hotbar slot has moved.
steps.stage_goal: Prove hotbar and inventory controls work in the new world.

steps.intent: Open the inventory screen.
steps.expected_observation: The Minecraft inventory/crafting screen is visible.
steps.stage_goal: Prove hotbar and inventory controls work in the new world.
